glossary.malignant: Cancerous: able to invade and spread to distant sites.
glossary.secondary tumour: A tumour formed by cancer cells that have spread from the original (primary) site.
glossary.genetic predisposition: An inherited tendency that raises the risk of developing a disease.
glossary.systemic symptoms: Whole-body symptoms such as weight loss, fatigue and fever.
glossary.bone tenderness: Pain when pressing over a bone.
glossary.neurological deficit: Loss of function of part of the nervous system, such as weakness or numbness.
glossary.focal neurological deficit: A problem affecting one specific area, such as one arm's weakness, pointing to a localised lesion.
glossary.spinal metastasis: Cancer that has spread to the vertebrae, risking spinal cord compression.
glossary.seizures: Episodes of abnormal electrical brain activity causing fits or altered awareness.
glossary.peritoneal cavity: The space inside the abdomen lined by the peritoneum.
glossary.ovarian carcinoma: Cancer of the ovary, which typically spreads across the peritoneum.
glossary.mesothelioma: Cancer of the lining of the lung or abdomen, usually from asbestos.
glossary.subarachnoid space: The fluid-filled space around the brain and spinal cord containing CSF.
glossary.CSF: Cerebrospinal fluid, which bathes the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.prostate cancer: Cancer of the prostate gland, which classically spreads to bone.
glossary.biopsy: Removal of a small tissue sample to look at under the microscope.
glossary.staging: Working out how far a cancer has spread, to guide treatment.
glossary.CNS: Central nervous system: the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.systemic therapy: Treatment that travels through the whole body, such as chemotherapy.
glossary.chemotherapy: Drugs that kill rapidly dividing cancer cells.
glossary.targeted therapy: Drugs aimed at a specific mutation or protein in the cancer.
glossary.oncology: The branch of medicine dealing with cancer.
glossary.steroids: Anti-inflammatory hormones, here used to reduce swelling around brain tumours.
glossary.cerebral oedema: Swelling of brain tissue, which raises pressure inside the skull.
glossary.prophylactic: Done to prevent something, here fixing a bone before it breaks.
glossary.cortical bone: The hard, dense outer layer of a bone that gives it strength.
glossary.weight-bearing pain: Pain on standing or walking on the affected limb.
glossary.capillary bed: A network of tiny vessels where blood exchanges substances with tissue; circulating cancer cells get trapped there.
glossary.portal venous drainage: Blood from the gut flowing via the portal vein to the liver first.
glossary.serosal surface: The smooth outer lining of organs inside a body cavity.
glossary.peritoneum: The thin membrane lining the abdominal cavity and covering its organs.
glossary.pleura: The thin membranes lining the lungs and inside of the chest wall.
